mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% over two consecutive quarters signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes despite CPIAUCSL > 3% for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where GDPC1 YoY falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and ultimately leads to higher input costs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during periods when UNRATE > 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in RSAFS over two months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes where FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and GDPC1 above their respective 12-month moving averages for three months signals strengthening housing and overall demand, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and GDPC1 > 12-month MA for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero during periods when both HOUST and GDPC1 are above their 12-month MA for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals labor market weakening, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where PAYEMS is below its 12-month MA for four months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL is below 2% for six consecutive months, the low-rate environment persists, supporting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for six months.
